The mirror carries no Old Testament, so OT quotations reuse the wording of an already-shipped Amharic work where one quotes the same verse (source_file names it) and are otherwise self_rendered in the 1962 register.

A `mined` row was checked by script against the finished text: every fragment of the epigraph is an exact substring of the 1962 NT verse (or of the cited corpus file) and of that block. Romans 10:14c is the one short row (18 characters): it is the whole clause the English quotes, verbatim.

The English epigraphs are KJV fragments cited `— from <Book> <chapter>`; per the shipped am children's editions each quotes the 1962 Bible's own wording for the part the English means, with … for words left out, and cites `— ከ<Book> <chapter>`. Isaiah 6:8b reuses daughters-of-the-king-3.am.json's two clauses (the nested ‹ › kept); Psalm 126:5 matches women-who-moved-heaven-2.am.json. Ecclesiastes 4:9 has no shipped Amharic rendering and is self_rendered.

Two body sentences echo a verse without quotation marks, as the English does: chapter 3's “Seek God's kingdom first” (Matthew 6:33a, abridged from the 1962 wording) and chapter 6's rich young man (Matthew 19:21, abridged).
